title: Swimming League Splashes Back With Star-Studded All-Star Match
summary:
Get ready for a splashy comeback. The International Swimming League, known as the ISL, is returning after a break of more than five years — and British swimming star Adam Ramsay-Peaty is leading the way.

The ISL is a fast-paced, team-based swimming league that first started in 2019. It stopped after 2021, because of the war in Ukraine and its effect on the league's backer, Ukrainian businessman Konstantin Grigorishin. Now it is back, starting with a big All-Star Match on 19 December at the Aquatics Centre in London.

Ramsay-Peaty, a three-time Olympic champion, will swim for the Commonwealth team, alongside South African swimmer Pieter Coetzee. The two were the first swimmers named for that team. Nine-time Olympic champion Caeleb Dressel was among the first names picked for the United States team.

The match will bring the world's best swimmers to London in four teams: Commonwealth, United States, Europe and Intercontinental. In all, 96 swimmers will race in 46 races packed into just two hours.

Ramsay-Peaty said it was important for athletes to support the league's return. He called it a nice rejuvenation and said big names and top performers were both needed to make it a success.

The league's organisers say they have learned from past money troubles. They plan to take things slowly rather than rushing ahead, and they hope the All-Star Match will be a stepping stone to a full return of the league. Plans for 2027 and beyond are already in the works.

Ramsay-Peaty did not swim in the 2021 season, even though he had been named captain of the London Roar team. This time, he is ready to dive back in.
why_it_matters: The league's return shows how a sports competition can come back after stopping, and whether it succeeds will depend on star athletes, careful planning and fans turning up to watch.
